title: AI Model Market Daily: Reading AI Models Like a Stock Market Board
gist: VIDRAFT_LAB's AI Model Market Daily rebuilds a daily composite AMM 100 ranking of AI models across money (OpenRouter token sales), intelligence (HF official boards, SuperCLUE, LMArena) and security (supply-chain, attack-resistance, agent-safety scans). Its 27 Nov 2026 snapshot shows different leaders on each axis (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on usage, Gemini 4 Argon on intelligence, Kimi K3.1 Pro on agent safety) and a Chinese-dominated open-weight top 100 (70 of 100).

insights.claim: On 27 November 2026, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash led OpenRouter token sales with 73.7T tokens over 7 days, a 38.3% share, while a different model (Gemini 4 Argon) led intelligence and another (Kimi K3.1 Pro) led agent safety.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Paid usage concentrates on cheap, good-enough Chinese models rather than benchmark leaders — monetization and SOTA are separate races.
insights.quote: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 led token sales with 73.7T tokens in 7 days (38.3% share)
insights.locator: Why one axis is not enough

insights.claim: Model selection by teams involves three distinct questions — whether anyone pays to use a model, how good it is under fair comparison, and whether it is safe to deploy and let act — so a single leaderboard is insufficient.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Use a money/intelligence/security triad when evaluating model-vendor traction instead of benchmark rank alone.
insights.quote: A single leaderboard answers a single question. Teams choosing a model ask three.
insights.locator: Why one axis is not enough

insights.claim: Across the top 300 Hugging Face models by downloads, combined 30-day downloads totalled 509.8 million as of 27 November 2026.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Gauge of open-weight distribution scale on Hugging Face; trackable daily via the public dataset.

themes.theme: Frontier SOTA ranking: Gemini on top

insights.claim: On the AMM 100 SOTA frontier ranking (closed and open models together) for 27 November 2026, Google's Gemini 4 models took the top three spots — Gemini 4 Argon 70.2, Gemini 4 Carbon 67.3, Gemini 4 Neon 66.4 — followed by Claude Fable 5 at 65.9 and GPT-6.1 Sol at 65.7.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Google holds a clear but narrow frontier lead; the gap between #4 and #5 (Anthropic vs OpenAI) is just 0.2 points.
insights.quote: Top five on 27 November: Gemini 4 Argon 70.2, Gemini 4 Carbon 67.3, Gemini 4 Neon 66.4, Claude Fable 5 65.9, GPT-6.1 Sol 65.7.
insights.locator: AMM 100 SOTA: closed and open together

insights.claim: The AMM 100 SOTA score uses the SuperCLUE total as a base scale and maps LMArena percentiles (overall, coding, hard prompts, expert, math) onto it by mean-sigma linking across 11 shared anchor models, then averages available sources.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Frontier rankings blending Chinese (SuperCLUE) and Western (LMArena) evals are sensitive to anchor choice; treat small gaps as noise.
insights.locator: AMM 100 SOTA: closed and open together

insights.claim: A frontier comparison requires sources that cover closed models because Hugging Face official benchmark boards list almost only open-weight models; mixing the two would rank closed models on missing data.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Hugging Face leaderboards structurally understate closed-model strength; don't read them as frontier rankings.
insights.quote: Mixing the two would rank closed models by missing data.

insights.claim: Of the AMM 100 Open top 100 open-weight models on 27 November 2026, 70 came from China, 21 from the United States, 5 from Korea, 2 from France and 2 from elsewhere.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Open-weight model leadership is overwhelmingly Chinese — a geopolitical and supply-chain consideration for enterprises adopting open models.
insights.quote: Of the open-weight top 100, 70 came from China, 21 from the United States, 5 from Korea, 2 from France and 2 from elsewhere.
insights.locator: AMM 100 Open: models you can actually download

insights.claim: The AMM 100 Open top five on 27 November 2026 were Kimi-K3.1-Pro (77.3), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (76.8), Inkling-2-Small (73.7), Kimi-K3 (73.2) and GLM-5.2 (71.1).
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: The Kimi line holds two of the top four open slots; watch Kimi and DeepSeek as the open-weight pace-setters.
insights.quote: Top five on 27 November: Kimi-K3.1-Pro 77.3, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 76.8, Inkling-2-Small 73.7, Kimi-K3 73.2, GLM-5.2 71.1.
insights.locator: AMM 100 Open: models you can actually download

insights.claim: AMM 100 Open weights performance across official Hugging Face boards at 0.50, benchmark wins at 0.15 and popularity (30-day ecosystem downloads including quantized and adapter derivatives, likes, trending) at 0.35, with a sqrt(min(N,10)/10) penalty so a model on few boards cannot rank high on one lucky result.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Popularity carries over a third of the open score, so ecosystem adoption (derivatives, quantizations) materially lifts rankings beyond raw benchmarks.
insights.quote: so one lucky board cannot carry a model
insights.locator: AMM 100 Open: models you can actually download

insights.claim: Strictly verifying that weights are downloadable from the developer's own Hugging Face organization confirmed only 203 of 218 models labelled 'open', and found 3 open models not labelled as such.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: 'Open' labels on leaderboards are ~7% unreliable — verify actual weight availability before betting on open-model supply.
insights.quote: A licence string or a leaderboard's "open" label alone does not count.
insights.locator: AMM 100 Open: models you can actually download

insights.claim: Among the top 300 Hugging Face models by downloads on 27 November 2026, supply-chain hygiene grades were A 193, B 92, C 15, D 0, F 0, but 21 still ship pickle files and 35 ship custom remote code.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Pickle and remote-code exposure persists in popular models — a tailwind for model-security scanning vendors and a diligence item for enterprise adopters.
insights.quote: 21 ship pickle files, 35 ship custom remote code
insights.locator: Security, in layers shown side by side

insights.claim: ViKernel Scanner tests across six attack domains on 21 open models given mock tools found an average attack success rate of 16.7%, falling to 0.0% with the ViKernel gate placed in front.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Agentic open models remain meaningfully exploitable unguarded; guardrail/gating layers are a plausible product category (note the claim comes from the gate's own ecosystem).
insights.quote: Average attack success 16.7%, and 0.0% with the ViKernel gate in front
insights.locator: Security, in layers shown side by side

insights.claim: On the Agent Safety Leaderboard, 19 models were measured and Kimi K3.1 Pro ranked first with a score of 98.6 on 27 November 2026.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: A Chinese open-weight model leading agent safety undercuts the assumption that open/Chinese models are the least safe agent choice.
insights.locator: Security, in layers shown side by side

insights.claim: AI Model Market Daily excludes Artificial Analysis (terms forbid a competing site) and OpenCompass (non-commercial clause) without written permission, signalling that benchmark-aggregator data is increasingly locked behind restrictive terms.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Benchmark data has commercial moat value; aggregators like Artificial Analysis are protecting it, constraining open competitors.
insights.quote: Artificial Analysis (terms forbid a competing site) and OpenCompass (non-commercial clause) are not used without written permission.
insights.locator: Rules that keep the board honest
